thread:
Sam: Noticed an uptick in tiny-pod scattering + eviction churn in ap-south1 for the last 30m. Looks like warmpool attach/timeouts + short NotReady blips.
Nina: Can you paste the event tail?
Sam: events: `Warning FailedAttachVolume 5m (x14 over 28m) attachdetach-controller attach failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded` and `Warning NodeNotReady 4m kubelet Node ap-south1-node-07 briefly NotReady`
Ravi: That pattern rings bell: when warmpool nodes flip briefly our scheduler's immediate eviction policy causes micro-rebalancing; tiny jobs get spread instead of waiting for node recovery. Fragmentation increases and we waste GPU-hours.
Cory: How bad is the cost hit?
Sam: delta on this pool ~9% extra compute last 2h (rough). If it persists could be hundreds of dollars/hr.
Ops-automation-bot: I can deploy a scoped scheduler config to reduce preemption aggressiveness and add a short node-failure backoff for a single nodepool. Suggest: nodeFlipGrace=25s, preemptPenalty=0.6.
Nina: Prefer we try a narrower fix first: bump kubelet `attachTimeout` for warmpool nodes to 40s (canary) and enable `delayed-taint-lift` so temporary NetworkUnavailable doesn't immediately cause eviction.
Ravi: Agreed. Also add a warmpool-specific scheduler predicate tweak: preferSpreadThreshold->lower to avoid aggressive scatter for tiny pods during transient shortages.
Sam: Plan: 1) Patch kubelet config on warmpool-canary-01 to attachTimeout=40s, 2) enable delayed-taint-lift for that nodepool, 3) apply scheduler softening on canary only, 4) monitor evictions, pod packing concentration, and cost for 20m, 5) rollback if regress.
Ops-automation-bot: Applying kubelet patch to warmpool-canary-01 now: `kubectl patch cm warmpool-canary-kubelet -n infra --patch '{"data":{"attachTimeout":"40s"}}'`
SRE-bot: Alert: evictions-high firing for cluster/ap-south1 (3m).
Nina: Kubelet rollout started on canary. Watching node metrics.
Sam: After 8m canary shows evictions -55% and packing index improved (more coalesced).
Ravi: Nice. We should capture NIC driver/kernel version on the impacted nodes and open a hardware ticket if we see repeats.
Cory: Once stabilized, let's document cost delta and add a scheduled test to simulate 10s NodeNotReady flaps in our CI scheduler tests.
Ops-automation-bot: Temporary scheduler config applied to canary; will auto-revert in 3h if not promoted.
Sam: Expanding to 2nd canary in ap-southeast1 in 10m if metrics stay green. Assigning follow-up: infra/warmpool-attach-investigation.
SRE-bot: Alert: evictions-high cleared for cluster/ap-south1.
